I took a look at [**`rockhoundgocody-spec/RHgo-v-2.0`**](https://github.com/rockhoundgocody-spec/RHgo-v-2.0). Here is a summary of the project architecture and its current state:

---

### Overview & Architecture
**RockHound-GO V2** is a field intelligence and geological adventure PWA/web app built with **React 18**, **Vite 6**, **Tailwind CSS**, **Three.js**, **Radix UI**, and the **Base44 SDK**.

The project is structured around the core field loop:
- **Explore** ([`Explore.jsx`](file:///tmp/rhgo-v-2.0/src/pages/Explore.jsx)): Map-based discovery (Leaflet / Google Maps), verified vs. unverified quick pins, hotspot accessibility, and sensitive coordinate protection.
- **Scan** ([`Scan.jsx`](file:///tmp/rhgo-v-2.0/src/pages/Scan.jsx)): Specimen classification with confidence ratings, hardness/acid test prompts, and ethical field actions (*Keep*, *Leave*, *Observe*).
- **GeoDex / Collection** ([`Collection.jsx`](file:///tmp/rhgo-v-2.0/src/pages/Collection.jsx)): Specimen archive with 3D viewing ([Three.js](file:///tmp/rhgo-v-2.0/package.json#L34)), rarity tiers, discovery chains, and Chronolith investigation cases.
- **Field & Offline**: Queued offline writes (`queueWrite`), field cache, and privacy-filtered coordinates.
- **Extended features**: Badges & XP, Expeditions, Community hub, Market, and Companion dashboards.
